clue.text: Mess up wrong raw material for French bread?

parts.note: bum as an adjective means bad or wrong, as in a bum note
blé is French for wheat, the raw material of a French loaf

explanation.surface: Someone ruins a batch of baguettes by using the wrong flour.
explanation.walkthrough: You need the French word blé (wheat); the question mark admits the definition-by-example of bread's raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: To bumble is to act clumsily and botch things, a synonym of messing up.

clue.text: Assert loan must be raised, causing quarrel

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising something lifts it so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to put a case is to assert it
a sub is an advance of money, a loan

explanation.surface: Someone insists a loan be increased, and a row breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust-up is informal for a violent quarrel or falling-out.

clue.text: Loose, run free, almost free

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the following word is dropped
the first free, read as a verb, sets the preceding word loose to rearrange itself

parts.note: the letters of run, rearranged
free means open, here cut short

explanation.surface: A runaway description: loose, running free, almost at liberty.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose is a verb here: climbers unrope when they release themselves from a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrope is to undo or loosen the rope tying climbers together.

clue.text: Quivering with 'it' — call me 'brassy' perhaps

indicators.note: something quivering is shaking and unsteady, so the letters jumble

parts.note: the letters of it, call and me together

explanation.surface: A trembling speaker brands themselves the brassy one, with 'it'.
explanation.walkthrough: Brassy is a single example of a metal-like quality, hence perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass is an alloy, so something brassy in sound or look is one kind of metal-like quality.

clue.text: Bullet blasted me, at rest — head of corps?

indicators.note: blasted means blown apart, so the following letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: a ball is an old word for a bullet, as in musket ball
the letters of me, at and rest, rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier shot and now lying still asks about the commander of the corps.
explanation.walkthrough: Corps suggests the army, but the corps de ballet is meant; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The ballet master trains and rehearses a company's dancers, so heads the corps de ballet.

clue.text: Watching hygiene after treatment, leaving hospital

indicators.note: treatment processes and changes things, so the letters are worked into a new order
leaving says one element departs from the word

parts.note: taken as written
H is the map abbreviation for hospital, removed

explanation.surface: Someone observes hygiene levels after a patient is treated and discharged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing means looking at closely, a synonym of watching.

clue.text: Splash pint? Pan's needed with this all over the place

definitions.text: Splash pint? Pan's needed with this all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the letters of both words, the pool to be rearranged
these letters, together with the answer, make up that pool, so they are taken away

explanation.surface: Slopped beer everywhere means someone needs a pan to catch it.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: Pan's plus the answer together rearrange to splash pint, and the whole clue pictures spilt liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Spilth is a literary word for something spilt, such as liquid slopped over the brim.

clue.text: Slap penetrated round performer's face

indicators.note: round says one part encircles another

parts.note: a ball that penetrated the pocket or net sank

indicators.note: a face is what is at the front, so only the opening letter counts

parts.note: the front letter of performer

explanation.surface: A slap goes straight through to an actor's face.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letter of performer sits inside the past tense meaning went in.
explanation.definitionFit: To spank is to slap, usually on the buttocks with the open hand.

clue.text: Dolly, say, one in cast performing

parts.note: a part is a role, one of those in a cast
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: Dolly is described as one of the cast in a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly looks like a doll or a film camera trolley, but it is the singer's first name; say marks her as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly Parton, the American country singer, is one bearer of the surname.

clue.text: Iris, tent shaking, was courting, with parts woven together

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of iris and tent, rearranged
to sue is an old word for to woo or court

explanation.surface: Iris's tent was shaking while someone came courting.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue in the old sense of paying court to someone, not litigation.
explanation.definitionFit: Intertissued is an archaic term for interwoven, of fabric with threads of different kinds.

clue.text: The endless beat (relating to the downbeat)

indicators.note: endless means without an end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
a tick is a beat, as of a clock, here losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A musical gloss: the endless beat, explained in brackets as the downbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: In prosody and music the thesis is the stressed or down beat, and thetic is its adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Thetic is the adjective from thesis, the term for the accented downbeat of a bar or metrical foot.

clue.text: Scottish hacks active with entertainers around

indicators.note: around says the entertainers surround the other piece

parts.note: hosts entertain guests
A is the grammar abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: Busy Scottish journalists are surrounded by entertainers.
explanation.walkthrough: Hacks suggests journalists, but here it is the verb-noun for coughs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoast is a Scots word for a cough, and a hack is a dry cough, so the plurals match.

clue.text: Feeble (lacking power) about rough sea, windy?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
rough water is churned up, so these letters are disordered
power is abbreviated P, and lacking it means that letter is removed

parts.note: puny means feeble; without its P it is the outer piece
the letters of sea, rearranged

explanation.surface: A weak sailor without strength is caught out on a stormy, windy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Windy is British slang for nervous or scared, not blowy; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Being windy in informal British use means frightened or nervous, which is to be anxious and unsettled.

clue.text: Villa, maybe one with central heating in the middle of Napoli

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
the middle of keeps only the central letters of the Italian city name

parts.note: the two central letters of the six
an means one
CH is the estate-agent abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: An estate agent lists a villa with central heating in central Naples.
explanation.walkthrough: Villa reads as a house, but it is Pancho Villa, the Mexican revolutionary leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancho Villa was the Mexican revolutionary general, so he is one person with that first name.

clue.text: Try untangling a pet in tropical climber

indicators.note: untangling rearranges strands, so these letters are sorted into a new order

parts.note: a judge tries a case, that is hears it
the letters of a and pet, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tries freeing a pet caught up in a jungle vine.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart pea, or balloon vine, is a tropical climbing plant with heart-marked seeds.

clue.text: In contact with the whole camp, virtually (12, three words)

parts.note: to can mean touching, as in cheek to cheek
all means the whole
to camp is to be in tents

explanation.surface: A holiday report: we were close to the entire campsite, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: To all intents and purposes is an idiom meaning in effect, practically, virtually.

clue.text: Winning, not fat? Rest one's weight as before

parts.note: a team ahead is up
lean means thin, not fat

explanation.surface: A slimmed-down winner settles back into the old stance.
explanation.walkthrough: As before marks the definition as an archaic usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplean is an obsolete verb meaning to lean or rest upon something.

clue.text: Mechanical spinning machine

parts.note: surface reading: the plain dictionary meaning, a device that spins thread; setter's reading: this is the puzzle's competition entry, which solvers were invited to clue themselves, so no wordplay is printed

explanation.walkthrough: This was Azed's clue-writing competition word: the printed clue is only the definition, and solvers had to supply their own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: From Latin filum (thread), the word names a machine that forms or spins threads.

clue.text: Who is fitted out with one? Hoplite was

definitions.text: Who is fitted out with one? Hoplite was

indicators.note: fitted out suggests putting together anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of both words, the pool to be rearranged
these letters, together with the answer, use up that pool, so they are taken away

explanation.surface: A quiz on armour: who carried this piece of kit? The Greek foot soldier did.
explanation.walkthrough: A compound anagram: who is plus the answer rearrange to hoplite was. Strictly, the pelta belonged to the lightly armed peltast rather than the hoplite.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelta is a small light shield of ancient Greek infantry, so the one the soldier is equipped with.

clue.text: High jinks? Not for civil servants as a whole

parts.note: anti means against, not for
CS is the abbreviation for Civil Service, the body of civil servants

explanation.surface: A disapproving question: horseplay is no way for government officials to behave.
explanation.definitionFit: Antics are playful or absurd capers, which is what high jinks means.

clue.text: Defective train going into sea

indicators.note: going into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
to train a gun is to aim it

explanation.surface: A faulty train runs off into the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Train looks like the railway noun, but it is the verb meaning point a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Maimed means mutilated or crippled, so damaged and defective.

clue.text: Plan to win nothing is admitted by club

indicators.note: being admitted by something means being let inside it

parts.note: a mere is a Maori war club
taken as written

explanation.surface: A club confesses its strategy is to win nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Club suggests a sports club or the card suit, but it is the Maori weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games such as solo whist, misère is a bid undertaking to take no tricks at all.

clue.text: Our distant ancestors, or a writer about them

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writer encloses the other piece

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
'em is the informal short form of them

explanation.surface: Our remote forebears, or else an author writing about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ape-men are the primitive hominids from which modern humans descend.

clue.text: Charger maybe in sparkling get-up, all but extremes

indicators.note: all but the extremes keeps everything except the two end letters

parts.note: a sparkly outfit is sequined, covered in spangles

explanation.surface: A warhorse is decked out in glittering show tack.
explanation.walkthrough: A charger is a cavalry horse, so one example of a horse-like creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A charger is a horse ridden in battle, and equine as a noun means a member of the horse family.

clue.text: Eye-catching feature in paper providing a little tonic

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prominent front-page story or display
second meaning: a small dash of a mixer added to a drink

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead feature acts as a pick-me-up for readers.
explanation.definitionFit: A splash is both a headline story given big display and a small quantity of liquid poured into a drink.

clue.text: French pronoun found in dictionary rather the worse for wear

indicators.note: found in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
il is French for he or it

explanation.surface: A French word turns up in a tattered old dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: The worse for wear describes the dictionary on the surface but here means tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled is informal for drunk, and being the worse for wear is a euphemism for drunkenness.

clue.text: What means game's up? Reverse of that for inventor

indicators.note: the reverse of that answer to the question reads it from its end back to its start

parts.note: no side is the referee's call ending a rugby match

explanation.surface: A riddle about the signal that ends a game, turned round to name an inventor.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the referee calls no side to end the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and a practical electric light bulb.

clue.text: Paper's edge to adorn with article from Paris

parts.note: to deck is to adorn
le is a French definite article

explanation.surface: Decorating the margin of a page with something bought in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckle edge is the rough, untrimmed edge of handmade paper.

clue.text: Transfer given upward move made stronger?

indicators.note: in a down entry an upward move turns the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: a decal is a transfer picture

explanation.surface: A transfer moved higher up is now stuck on more firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark fits the sense of a drink fortified with spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A laced drink has had alcohol added to it, so it is made more potent.

clue.text: First character to perform admits stiff dressage manoeuvre

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the name of the first letter of perform, spelt out
in Chambers, sad describes heavy, stiff, badly risen dough

explanation.surface: An opening act takes on a rigid horse-riding routine.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter P is written as its spoken name, pee, to hold the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pesade is the dressage movement in which the horse rears on its hind legs.

clue.text: A lustiness unbridled, I see — could be this

definitions.text: A lustiness unbridled, I see — could be this

indicators.note: unbridled means unrestrained and wild, so the letters run loose into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
I and C, the letter that sounds like see

explanation.surface: An observer notes that unchecked lust might deserve this label.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: someone of unbridled lustiness could well be called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensualistic means given to pleasures of the senses, which describes unrestrained lust.

clue.text: Resident alien once tucked into ale, terribly sick-making

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters are mangled
tucked into places one piece snugly inside the other

parts.note: the letters of ale, rearranged and split around the other piece
a metic was a resident foreigner in an ancient Greek city

explanation.surface: A foreigner drinks so much ale that the drinker turns terribly ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Emetical is an old form of emetic, causing vomiting.

clue.text: Which secret enemy's grasped? It's extracted from tar

indicators.note: grasped means held within, so the answer is held inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A spy novel line: which hidden foe's plot has been understood?
explanation.definitionFit: Retene is a hydrocarbon obtained from pine tar and other resinous distillates.

clue.text: Solid alcohol that gets ostler reeling

indicators.note: reeling means staggering about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: an ostler is a stableman at an inn

explanation.surface: Strong drink that leaves the inn's stableman staggering.
explanation.walkthrough: Solid alcohol sounds like hard liquor, but it is chemistry: an alcohol in solid form.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterols, such as cholesterol, are a class of solid steroid alcohols found in animal and plant tissue.

clue.text: Hardened revolutionary pursuing name in European group

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: EU is the European Union
N is the abbreviation for name
a Red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: A seasoned radical follows a name on a European committee list.
explanation.walkthrough: Pursuing means coming after, so the revolutionary goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Enured is a variant spelling of inured, accustomed and toughened by exposure to hardship.

clue.text: What'll launch rocket aloft, we hear, and deny malfunctioning

indicators.note: malfunctioning means not working properly, so the letters go out of order
we hear points to a word as spoken rather than as spelt

parts.note: aloft means high up, and the two letters sound the same
the letters of deny, rearranged

explanation.surface: Mission control reports a rocket going up and a refusal to fail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydyne is a liquid rocket propellant, used in early American launch vehicles.
